rationale.conceptual: DPOSE is an established but non-trivial method (shallow ensembles with weight sharing and NLL loss) that must be correctly integrated into SchNet. Understanding the model modification, loss function, and evaluation logic requires careful implementation, but no novel algorithm derivation or deep mathematical innovation is needed.
rationale.execution: The reproduction involves a multi-stage pipeline: training QM9-SE from scratch (1000 epochs), fine-tuning OC20-SE and AuMD-SE, and evaluating all three models. Orchestration of data loading, environment setup (SchNet, pretrained checkpoint), and collection of variance metrics is moderately involved but uses standard deep learning libraries.

difficulty.reasoning: DPOSE integration into SchNet requires implementing a non-trivial architecture (64 shallow heads, NLL loss) and performing three separate trainings on different datasets; the pipeline involves multiple stages but no extreme complexity.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Training on QM9 (130k molecules, batch 100, 1000 epochs) and fine-tuning on OC20 intermetallic slabs and gold bulk structures require a GPU; QM9 dataset ~3.4 GB, OC20 subset ~10–20 GB, Gold dataset small; SchNet with 64 heads needs ~16 GB VRAM.
